title: add-importance-weighted-cohort-smoother-and-latency-tempered-ci-hook
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: CI-driven prompt-set regression gates have high sensitivity to rare prompt failures and can generate noisy alerts when transient latency spikes or skewed sampling amplify low-impact differences. This PR introduces an importance-weighted cohort smoother plus a latency-tempered CI hook that reduces spurious failures by downweighting historic low-importance samples and attenuating the effect of high-latency outliers in quality gates. Design summary: 1) importance_weights module computes per-prompt weights using a configurable recency window, exposure frequency, and an inverse-latency factor; 2) cohort_smoother aggregates eval metrics (accuracy, BLEU-like similarity, and semantic similarity) using the IW estimator with bootstrap confidence intervals; 3) latency_tempered_hook plugs into the existing CI eval runner and applies a sliding-temporal dampening factor to the gate decision when latency variance exceeds threshold; 4) a fallback soft-fail path is provided to create a triage ticket instead of failing main pipelines for marginal regressions. Changes include implementation, unit and integration tests, docs, and a small CI adapter. Testing & rollout: unit tests and deterministic sim harness added; staged rollout enabled via feature flag eval.iw_smoother.enabled:false by default; nightly CI will opt-in on a 10% canary for 48 hours before global enablement. Local test instructions: pytest tests/test_iw_smoother.py::TestIWWeighting::test_bootstrap_estimator --runslow and run scripts/ci_eval_runner --hook latency_tempered_hook --sample-size 200. Backwards compatibility: the hook is opt-in and defaults to no-op when importance weights are unset; it does not change stored eval artifacts format. Related work: builds on ENG-3429 (cohort sampling refactor) and ENG-3498 (CI gate abstractions). Release notes: Add importance-weighted cohort smoother and latency-tempered CI hook to reduce CI noise from transient latency spikes and rare prompt samples.
